name: Germany
prPathwayNote: EU Blue Card eligibility after graduation; permanent residency possible in 21–27 months with German language proficiency.
languageRequired: English (IELTS 6.5) for English-taught master's; German A1/B1 highly recommended for student jobs and daily life.
keyPros: Nearly zero tuition fees at public universities
18-month job seeker visa after graduation
Strong engineering, IT and manufacturing industry
Direct permanent residency pathway via EU Blue Card
keyCons: High competition for English-taught master's seats
German bureaucracy and embassy visa appointment wait times
German language needed for social integration and local student jobs
overview: Germany is the #1 choice for Bangladeshi engineering and science graduates seeking tuition-free world-class education with clear, structured permanent residency pathways.

The embassy digitally reviews your documents to ensure completeness before issuing an in-person appointment slot in Dhaka.
Attend your in-person appointment at the German Embassy Visa Section in Baridhara, Dhaka with all original attested certificates and biometric photos.

commonFaqs.question: How does the new German online visa application process work for Bangladeshi students?
commonFaqs.answer: The German Federal Foreign Office now uses the online Consular Services Portal (Auslandsportal at digital.diplo.de). You complete the visa form online and upload all required documents (admission letter, Sperrkonto blocked account confirmation, attested transcripts, CV, and motivation letter) for digital pre-checking. Once the embassy completes the digital pre-check, you are allocated an appointment in Dhaka to submit biometrics and show your original papers.

commonFaqs.question: Is German language knowledge mandatory for applying to German universities?
commonFaqs.answer: No. There are over 1,500 English-taught master programs in Germany where only an IELTS score (typically 6.5) is required. However, learning A1/A2 German before departure is strongly recommended for part-time student jobs and daily life.

commonFaqs.question: Are public universities in Germany really 100% tuition-free?
commonFaqs.answer: Yes. In 15 out of 16 German federal states, public universities charge zero tuition fees for all students regardless of nationality. You only pay a semester administrative fee of €150-€350, which usually includes free regional public transit.

commonFaqs.question: Can I apply to Germany with a study gap?
commonFaqs.answer: German universities accept study gaps if you provide valid proof of professional work experience, publications, or career progression related to your chosen field of study.

Generous 28 hours/week part-time work permit during terms
High graduate employment rate due to aging population and talent shortage
Extremely safe, technologically advanced society

Hierarchical academic lab culture (Sensei professor endorsement mandatory)
High upfront rent and apartment guarantor fees in central Tokyo
overview: Japan offers generous government scholarships (MEXT), world-leading research laboratories, and immediate post-graduate hiring for STEM and international business graduates.

commonFaqs.question: Can I study in Japan without knowing Japanese?
commonFaqs.answer: Yes! Japan offers English-Degree Programs (Global 30 and university-specific tracks) where courses are 100% taught in English. You only need an IELTS (6.0-6.5) or TOEFL score for admission.

commonFaqs.question: What is the MEXT Scholarship and how can Bangladeshi students apply?
commonFaqs.answer: MEXT is the Japanese Government Scholarship covering 100% tuition, round-trip airfare, and a monthly stipend of ¥143,000-¥145,000. Bangladeshi students can apply through the Embassy Recommendation (announced by Ministry of Education around April/May) or directly through University Recommendation.

commonFaqs.question: How many hours can international students work in Japan?
commonFaqs.answer: Students can legally work up to 28 hours per week during academic terms, and up to 40 hours per week during official semester vacations.

H-1B visa lottery system creates post-OPT uncertainty
Strict in-person consular visa interview (F-1 214b non-immigrant intent)
overview: The premier destination for funded graduate research in STEM, offering Graduate Teaching and Research Assistantships that make full degrees essentially free for strong academic profiles.

Focus interview answers on academic intent, research plans, and definite career return to Bangladesh.

commonFaqs.question: How do Bangladeshi students get fully funded in the US for Master and PhD?
commonFaqs.answer: In the US, STEM graduate students often receive Graduate Teaching Assistantships (TA) or Graduate Research Assistantships (RA). An assistantship waives 100% of your tuition fees and pays a monthly stipend of ,800 to ,800 in exchange for 20 hours/week of academic work.

commonFaqs.question: Can I stay and work in the US after graduation?
commonFaqs.answer: Yes. Graduates from STEM-designated degree programs receive a total of 36 months (3 years) of post-study work authorization under STEM OPT without needing an immediate H-1B visa sponsor.

commonFaqs.question: What is the most common reason for US student visa refusal in Dhaka?
commonFaqs.answer: The most frequent refusal reason under INA 214(b) is failing to demonstrate strong non-immigrant intent and clear career plans in Bangladesh, or giving rehearsed, memorized answers during the 2-minute consular interview.

name: Canada
prPathwayNote: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) leads directly to Canadian Experience Class (Express Entry) and Provincial Nominee Programs (PNP).

keyPros: Clear, transparent post-graduation work permit (PGWP up to 3 years)
Direct permanent residency pathways through Express Entry & PNP
24 hours per week off-campus work allowed during academic sessions
Spouse open work permit options for master's and doctoral students
keyCons: High GIC cost requirement upfront
Severe housing shortages and rising rents in Toronto and Vancouver
Recent national caps on international student study permits
overview: Canada remains a top choice for Bangladeshi families seeking quality North American degrees backed by reliable post-study work permits and established economic immigration streams.

Undergo upfront medical examination at an approved IOM / Green Crescent panel clinic.
Include strong proof of funds and explanation of tuition remitted via Bangladeshi AD bank student file.

commonFaqs.question: What is a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) for Canada?
commonFaqs.answer: Under current IRCC regulations, all undergraduate and non-degree students must obtain a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) from the provincial government via their university before submitting their study permit application. Master and PhD students are exempt.

commonFaqs.question: Can Bangladeshi students work off-campus in Canada?
commonFaqs.answer: Yes. International students enrolled full-time can work up to 24 hours per week off-campus during academic terms, and full-time during scheduled breaks.

commonFaqs.question: Is it easy to obtain Canadian Permanent Residency (PR) after graduation?
commonFaqs.answer: Graduates receive a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) of up to 3 years. Canadian study and work experience award high points in Express Entry (Canadian Experience Class) and Provincial Nominee Programs (PNP).

languageRequired: English (IELTS Academic 6.0–7.0 / UKVI IELTS; MOI accepted by select universities).

2-year unsponsored Graduate Route visa to work in any job sector
Historic, globally respected university prestige and alumni networks
Established Bangladeshi diaspora, Halal food availability, and cultural familiarity
keyCons: High tuition and London living costs
Skilled Worker visa minimum salary thresholds recently raised
Strict 28-day bank holding period requirement for visa filing
overview: The 1-year master's format in the UK allows Bangladeshi students to finish their postgraduate qualification and enter the job market twice as fast as in North America.

commonFaqs.question: How long can I work in the UK after graduating?
commonFaqs.answer: Under the UK Graduate Route, international graduates can live and work in the UK for 2 years (3 years for PhD graduates) at any skill level without needing an employer sponsorship.

commonFaqs.question: Can I bring my spouse/dependents to the UK on a student visa?
commonFaqs.answer: Only students enrolled in postgraduate research programs (PhD and research-based Master) or government-sponsored scholarship holders can bring dependents to the UK.

commonFaqs.question: Can I apply to UK universities without IELTS?
commonFaqs.answer: Some UK universities accept Medium of Instruction (MOI) letters from recognized Bangladeshi universities or English marks from HSC (e.g. 70%+ in English). However, having IELTS 6.5 ensures the highest visa success rate.

commonFaqs.answer: The GS requirement replaced the GTE test. Applicants must provide targeted written statements demonstrating their academic background, career relevance, value to their future in Bangladesh, and reasons for choosing Australia.

commonFaqs.question: What are the part-time work rights in Australia?
commonFaqs.answer: International students can work up to 48 hours per fortnight (24 hours/week on average) while their course is in session, and unlimited hours during semester breaks.

commonFaqs.question: What are the post-graduation work rights in Finland?
commonFaqs.answer: Finland grants an exceptional 2-year post-study job seeker residence permit after graduation. Time spent on a student permit counts at 50% toward the 4-year permanent residency (PR) requirement.

commonFaqs.question: What is Ireland Third Level Graduate Scheme (Stamp 1G)?
commonFaqs.answer: Non-EU Master and PhD graduates receive a 24-month (2-year) Stamp 1G stay-back option to work full-time (up to 40 hours/week) in Ireland, which frequently leads to a Critical Skills Employment Permit.

commonFaqs.question: Why is Ireland popular for tech and pharmaceutical graduates from Bangladesh?
commonFaqs.answer: Ireland hosts the European headquarters of Google, Meta, Apple, Pfizer, and Intel, creating robust graduate hiring opportunities in Dublin, Cork, and Galway.

commonFaqs.question: How long does the Malaysian student visa take from Dhaka?
commonFaqs.answer: EMGS processing takes approximately 3-4 weeks for the electronic Visa Approval Letter (e-VAL), followed by 5-7 working days for the Single Entry Visa (SEV) at the Malaysian High Commission in Dhaka.

commonFaqs.question: What is the Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)?
commonFaqs.answer: GKS covers full tuition, roundtrip airfare, 1 year of Korean language training, and a monthly stipend of 1,000,000 KRW. Bangladeshi candidates apply either via the Embassy track (UGC circular) or University track.

commonFaqs.question: Can I work part-time while studying in South Korea?
commonFaqs.answer: Yes, after completing 1 semester (6 months), students can work up to 20-25 hours per week with permission from their university international office and local immigration office.

commonFaqs.question: How does the Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship work in Bangladesh?
commonFaqs.answer: The Hungarian Government awards 140 fully funded scholarships to Bangladeshi students annually through a bilateral agreement with the Ministry of Education Bangladesh / UGC. It covers 100% tuition, dormitory accommodation or allowance, and monthly stipend.

commonFaqs.question: What is the cost of studying in Hungary if self-funded?
commonFaqs.answer: Hungary is one of the most affordable European destinations. Tuition ranges from €2,500 to €5,000 per year, and living costs in Budapest are approximately 60,000 to 90,000 BDT per month.

commonFaqs.question: What are regional DSU scholarships in Italy?
commonFaqs.answer: Regional Italian government scholarships (e.g. DSU Toscana, EDISU Piemonte, LazioDisco) are awarded based on family financial need (ISEE Parificato). They provide 100% tuition waiver, free student canteen meals, and a cash stipend of €5,000-€7,500/year.

commonFaqs.question: What is the CIMEA comparability certificate for Italy?
commonFaqs.answer: CIMEA is an official verification statement of your academic qualifications required by Italian universities and the Italian Embassy in Dhaka, replacing or supplementing the traditional Declaration of Value (DOV).

commonFaqs.question: Are there low-tuition public universities in France?
commonFaqs.answer: French public universities are heavily subsidized by the French government. Non-EU students at universities applying differentiated fees pay €2,770/year for Bachelor degrees and €3,770/year for Master degrees.

commonFaqs.question: What is the CAF housing assistance subsidy in France?
commonFaqs.answer: All students in France (including international students) are eligible for CAF (Caisse d Allocations Familiales), a government subsidy that refunds 20% to 40% of your monthly room rent.

commonFaqs.question: Can international students work in Poland?
